title: Dates: day-month order and 'el … de …'
observed_issue: Uses month-day order or ordinals for all days ('el primero/segundo/tercero de…')
native_expectation: Day before month with cardinals: 'el quince de marzo'; only the 1st may be ordinal in some regions ('el primero', LatAm) vs cardinal 'el uno de' (Spain). Year as full number: 'dos mil veinticinco', not 'veinte veinticinco'

title: Number gender agreement with nouns
observed_issue: Uses invariant 'uno/veintiuno' before feminine nouns: 'veintiuno tarjetas', 'uno reserva'
native_expectation: Apocope/feminine: 'una reserva', 'veintiún euros', 'veintiuna tarjetas', 'doscientas millas/personas' vs 'doscientos euros'

title: Native airline/telecom/retail terms vs English calques
observed_issue: Uses anglicisms/calques: 'cancelar mi booking', 'el refund', 'hacer un return', 'mi data plan', 'check-in' said English-style
native_expectation: 'mi reserva', 'el reembolso/la devolución', 'una devolución', 'mi tarifa de datos/plan de datos', 'facturación' o naturalized 'el check-in'; 'reembolso' not 'refund'

title: Alphanumeric codes: native letter names + spelling alphabet
observed_issue: Spells letters with English names ('A B C' as /ei bi si/) or uses NATO/English spelling words ('B as in Bravo')
native_expectation: Spanish letter names ('be', 'uve/ve', 'i griega/ye', 'hache', 'jota', 'doble u') and Spanish clarifiers: 'B de Barcelona', 'N de Navarra'. Double letter: 'doble ele' or 'dos eles'

title: Default to usted in service calls
observed_issue: Defaults to tú (English-centric, treats all 'you' as neutral), or mixes tú and usted within one turn
native_expectation: Spanish-speaking caller and agent use usted throughout a cold service call: '¿Me podría ayudar?', 'Quisiera consultar...'; verbs, clitics and possessives stay 3rd person ('su reserva', 'le confirmo'). Switching to tú reads as rude or non-native

title: Native hesitation markers
observed_issue: Inserts English-shaped fillers ('um', 'uh') or none at all; overuses 'pues' mechanically
native_expectation: Uses 'eh…', 'este…' (LatAm), 'o sea', 'a ver', 'pues nada', 'es que…' to preface a problem ('Es que no me llegó el reembolso')

title: Region-locked lexicon must stay consistent
observed_issue: Mixes Peninsular and LatAm markers in one persona: 'vale' + 'ahorita' + 'coger el vuelo' + 'vosotros' alongside 'ustedes'
native_expectation: Stays coherent: Spain → 'vale', 'coger un vuelo', 'vosotros', 'móvil'; LatAm → 'okay/dale', avoids 'coger' (vulgar in much of LatAm; use 'tomar/abordar'), 'ustedes', 'celular', 'ahorita'

title: Service-call politeness routines
observed_issue: Over-thanks in English pattern ('Thank you so much' → 'Muchas gracias por tu tiempo') or uses bare imperatives that sound brusque
native_expectation: '¿Sería tan amable de…?', 'Cuando pueda', 'Si no es molestia', 'Disculpe que le moleste'; closes with 'Muy amable, gracias' / 'Que tenga buen día'. Requests softened with conditional/imperfect

title: 'Esperar' for hold, not calque of 'hold on'
observed_issue: Calques 'hold on' / 'let me check' as 'sostener' or 'déjame chequear' (chequear is an anglicism flagged in formal register)
native_expectation: 'Un momento, por favor', 'Permítame que lo compruebo/lo reviso', 'No cuelgue, por favor'. 'comprobar/revisar/consultar' over 'chequear'

title: Ser/estar and por/para distinctions
observed_issue: Confuses ser/estar ('mi cuenta es bloqueada' instead of estar) and por/para ('gracias para tu ayuda')
native_expectation: 'mi cuenta está bloqueada' (state), 'el cargo es de 20 euros'; 'gracias por su ayuda', 'es para el día quince'. These map poorly from English and are high-tell errors

title: Gender of nouns and adjective/article agreement
observed_issue: Mis-genders or mis-agrees, esp. tricky nouns: 'la problema', 'el reserva', 'un orden' (for sequence), wrong adjective ending 'la vuelo cancelada'
native_expectation: el problema, la reserva, el vuelo cancelado, la tarjeta bloqueada; agreement is automatic across article+noun+adjective+participle

title: Clitic/possessive agreement with usted
observed_issue: Keeps usted in the verb but slips to informal clitics/possessives: 'le confirmo tu correo', 'te mando su factura'
native_expectation: Person is consistent: 'le confirmo su correo', 'le envío su factura'. Mixed te/su in one breath instantly flags a non-native

title: Verbalizing the email @ and dot
observed_issue: Says 'at' / 'arroba' inconsistently and reads '.com' as 'dot com' or 'punto com' with English 'com'
native_expectation: '@' = 'arroba', '.' = 'punto', '_' = 'guion bajo', '-' = 'guion' (or 'guion medio'); 'gmail.com' = 'gmail punto com'. e.g. 'juan arroba gmail punto com'

title: Translationese for 'I'd like / I need'
observed_issue: Calques English politeness: 'Me gustaría a...', 'Necesito que tú...', overuses 'Puedo tener...' ('Can I have...')
native_expectation: Uses native softeners: 'Quería consultar...', 'Quisiera...', 'Le quería preguntar...', 'A ver si me puede ayudar'. 'Quería' (imperfect) is the idiomatic service opener, not 'quiero'

title: Confirmation backchannels
observed_issue: Translates 'okay/right/got it' as repeated 'bien'/'okay' or silence
native_expectation: 'vale' (Spain) / 'dale', 'ya', 'ajá', 'de acuerdo', 'perfecto', 'correcto'; affirming comprehension with 'sí, sí' doubled is natural, not emphatic

title: Calque
observed_issue:
The use of "subir" (En., "go up") sounds like a calque (assuming the origianl was "upgrade"). Additionally, uses "para" instead of "a." Another anglicism is "business," but this is used more deliberately, meaning it was probably an attempt to sound more organic by the IA.

The use of "compensación" sounds like a calque (assuming the original was "compensation").
native_expectation: A native speaker would probably say something like "pasar" (En., "change," in this context) instead of the calque-sounding "subir," or say something more descriptive.
example:
"quiero subir a business para todos los pasajeros." -> "quiero pasar a business a todos los pasajeros."

"compensación" -> something like "reembolso" or "devolución."

"la trascripción está incompleta" -> "no he terminado de deletrear" or something along those lines.

title: Repetitive utterance starter
observed_issue: Repetitive use of the utterance starter.
native_expectation: A human would use a variety of utterance starters.
example: "si, dale" or "buenos días."

title: Forced idioms
observed_issue: The caller uses idioms that are too informal.
native_expectation: A human is unlikely to use those idioms given the context of the call.
example: "me tiene podrida," "stoy re caliente."

title: Too patient
observed_issue: The AI caller is too patient when the agent asks to spell something and then proceeds to give an example.
native_expectation: A human would interrupt and start spelling what's being asked.

title: Repetitive interruptions
observed_issue: Background noise prevents the agent from interacting when the the caller is not speaking, and when the agent can speak, the caller interrupts by saying the same phrase. This is the dynamic of the entire conversation.
native_expectation: A human would say something different each time (specially after noting that the agent is struggling to speak) and/or hang up the phone.
example: N/A

title: Self-talk
observed_issue: The caller responds to nothing (replies to the agent when the agent hasn't said anything).
native_expectation: It follows from "How the IA caller sounds non-native."
example: N/A

title: Airport abbreviations
observed_issue: When the user instructions refer to airports/places by their abbreviations, similarly, the AI caller spells abbreviations.
native_expectation: A human would refer to airports by their cities and/or states.
example: "de IAH a SEA" -> "de Houston a Seattle."

title: Verb misconjugation
observed_issue: Conjugates verb "acordar" incorrectly.
native_expectation: Conjugates verb "acordar" correctly.
example: "no me lo acuerdo bien" -> "no me acuerdo bien" or "no lo recuerdo bien."
human_note: People often make this kind of error -- it's just rare.

title: Missing natural Hindi fillers/hedges
observed_issue: Uses no fillers or only English 'um/uh'; produces clean, written-style sentences.
native_expectation: Sprinkles 'मतलब', 'वो क्या है ना', 'actually', 'बस', 'थोड़ा', 'ऐसा है कि', 'यानी'. Hedged openings like 'वो क्या है ना, मेरी flight...' are very common.

title: Dates and money in native form
observed_issue: Says dates in English order/month names with ordinals ('April fifteenth') or full Hindi cardinals for rupees with paise.
native_expectation: Day before month, cardinal day: 'पंद्रह अप्रैल' / '15 तारीख़'; money in rupees with लाख/हज़ार: 'साढ़े तीन हज़ार', 'पाँच हज़ार रुपये'. Uses तारीख़ for 'date' and the lakh system.

title: Phone/PNR digit grouping and 'double'
observed_issue: Reads long numbers as one big Hindi cardinal ('छियानवे करोड़...') or strictly digit-by-digit in Hindi without natural pairing and English 'double'.
native_expectation: Reads phone numbers in 2–3 digit chunks, often code-switching to English digits, and uses 'double' for repeats: 'double nine', 'नौ-आठ-सात... double-two'.

title: Translationese for 'I want to / I would like to'
observed_issue: Calques English politeness: 'मैं चाहूँगा कि...', or stiff 'मुझे ... करने की इच्छा है'.
native_expectation: Uses 'मुझे ... करना है' / '... करवाना है': 'मुझे flight cancel करवानी है'. The causative करवाना (get it done by someone) is the natural service-call verb, not plain करना.

title: Account/telecom/retail terms kept in English
observed_issue: Translates account→खाता, password→कूटशब्द, recharge→पुनःभरण, order→आदेश, network→संजाल.
native_expectation: Says account, password/OTP, recharge, plan, order, delivery, network, balance, data in English: 'मेरा OTP नहीं आया', 'recharge fail हो गया', 'order deliver नहीं हुआ'.

title: Backchannels जी / हाँ जी / अच्छा
observed_issue: Acknowledges with bare 'हाँ' or English 'okay/yes', missing the ubiquitous जी-based backchannels.
native_expectation: Uses 'जी', 'जी हाँ', 'हाँ जी', 'अच्छा अच्छा', 'ठीक है जी', 'जी बिल्कुल' as continuers. 'जी?' alone signals 'sorry, come again?'.

title: Request framing — ज़रा/please and indirect requests
observed_issue: Issues direct imperatives translated from English ('मेरी booking cancel करो') without softeners, or overuses a literal 'कृपया'.
native_expectation: Softens with 'ज़रा', 'please' (English), and modal 'क्या आप ... सकते हैं?': 'ज़रा check कर दीजिए ना'. कृपया is written-register; spoken callers prefer ज़रा + please.

title: 'Problem/issue' and complaint vocabulary
observed_issue: Uses समस्या/कठिनाई for every problem and शिकायत-दर्ज stiffly.
native_expectation: Says 'problem'/'issue'/'दिक्कत'/'परेशानी': 'मुझे एक दिक्कत आ रही है', 'issue ये है कि...', 'complaint करनी है'. समस्या is fine but दिक्कत/issue dominate calls.

title: Time of day and relative time
observed_issue: Uses 24-hour or stiff 'पूर्वाह्न/अपराह्न'; literal 'morning ten o'clock'.
native_expectation: 12-hour with सुबह/शाम/रात/दोपहर and बजे: 'सुबह दस बजे', 'शाम साढ़े छह बजे'; relative time 'परसों', 'अगले हफ़्ते', 'कल'.

title: Over-translating domain nouns into shuddh Hindi
observed_issue: Renders core service terms in pure/Sanskritized Hindi — उड़ान (flight), आरक्षण (booking), निरस्तीकरण (cancellation), धनवापसी (refund) — sounding like a news broadcast, not a phone customer.
native_expectation: Keeps these in English inside a Hindi matrix: 'मेरी flight cancel हो गई', 'booking change करनी है', 'refund कब आएगा'. Real callers say flight/booking/cancel/refund/seat/PNR in English and inflect Hindi around them.

title: Verbalizing email symbols @ . _ -
observed_issue: Speaks symbols in literal Hindi calques (डॉट as बिंदु, underscore as अधोरेखा, hyphen as योजक) or omits them.
native_expectation: Uses the conventional spoken-English tokens embedded in Hindi: 'एट द रेट' (or 'एट') for @, 'डॉट' for ., 'अंडरस्कोर' for _, 'डैश/हाइफ़न' for -, and 'gmail डॉट com'. Local-part letters spelled in English alphabet names.

title: Honorific-plural verb agreement with आप
observed_issue: Pairs आप with singular verb endings ('आप बता', 'आप कर सकता है') or mixes आप and तुम; uses तुम/तू toward an agent.
native_expectation: आप always takes plural agreement and -इए imperative: 'आप बता सकते हैं', 'ज़रा देख लीजिए', 'आप बताइए'. Customer↔agent stays mutually आप; तुम/तू would be rude.

title: 'Has happened / got done' aspect with हो गया
observed_issue: Uses plain present/past calqued from English ('मेरा payment fail है', 'booking cancel है') instead of the resultative.
native_expectation: Marks completed events with हो गया/गई: 'payment fail हो गया', 'booking cancel हो गई', 'पैसे कट गए'. 'कट गए' (money got deducted) is the idiomatic complaint phrasing.

title: Over-formal Sanskritized connectives
observed_issue: Uses written-register connectives: 'इसलिए', 'परंतु', 'तथा', 'अतः', 'धन्यवाद' stiffly throughout.
native_expectation: Spoken register uses 'तो', 'लेकिन/पर', 'क्योंकि', 'और', and ends with 'thank you'/'शुक्रिया' rather than formal धन्यवाद; परंतु/तथा/अतः sound like a textbook.

title: Opening and closing routines
observed_issue: Opens with a literal 'नमस्ते, मैं आपकी कैसे मदद कर सकता हूँ' from the customer side, or closes with bare English 'bye'.
native_expectation: Caller opens 'हाँ जी, हेलो' / 'जी, बात हो रही है ...?' and states the issue; closes 'ठीक है जी, थैंक्यू'. 'हेलो' (not नमस्ते) is the default phone opener.

title: Spelling alphanumeric codes (PNR) letter by letter
observed_issue: Pronounces a PNR/booking code as a word or uses Hindi letter names (क ख ग), with no spelling-alphabet anchoring.
native_expectation: Spells codes using English letter names with Hindi connectors: 'capital A, फिर 7, Z, K'; agents confirm 'Z for zebra?'-style anchors in English. Codes use the Roman alphabet, not Devanagari.

observed_issue: "इस user id से आपका प्रोफ़ाइल ढूंढता/ढूंढती हूँ।", "माफ़ कमैं समझ सकता/सकती हूँ "

native_expectation: Normally when talking about air tickets we use full cities name like "आपकी फ्लाइट लॉस एंजिल्स से लास वेगास की है"

observed_issue: बहुत ख़ुशी हुई मदद करके। आप आराम से email का इंतज़ार करें।
native_expectation: Locals would say " मुझे ख़ुशी हुई मदद आपकी करके, धन्यवाद"

native_expectation: common hinid phrase will be "जरा रुकिए" or "एक मिनट" also greeting wont have ji as suffix

native_expectation: A normal human would interrupt to correct if wrong

observed_issue: In between conversation it uses words like "Mane"
native_expectation: local would use "मुझे"

title: Indirectness and -는데요 trailing
observed_issue: States needs as complete blunt sentences ('환불해 주세요. 이유는…') in English problem-then-request order
native_expectation: Trails off with -는데요 / -아서요 leaving the request implied (어제 결제가 두 번 됐는데요…). This collaborative incompleteness is core to Korean service talk.

title: Request softeners and grammar of asking
observed_issue: Direct calques: '도와줄 수 있어요?' / uses 원하다 for 'I want' (저는 환불을 원해요)
native_expectation: Native: 환불 받고 싶은데요 / 환불 좀 해 주세요 / 확인 좀 부탁드려요. The trailing -는데요 to soften and 좀 as a softener are essential; 원하다 sounds like a translated demand.

title: Over- or mis-applied subject honorific -시-
observed_issue: Sprinkles -시- everywhere or applies it to the customer's own actions (제가 예약하셨어요)
native_expectation: Customer never honorifics their own verbs (제가 예약했어요); applies -시- only to the agent/third party. Agent uses -시- on the customer's actions (고객님 예약하셨어요?).

title: Native hesitation fillers
observed_issue: Inserts English-shaped fillers or none; over-clean speech
native_expectation: Uses 그…, 저기요, 음…, 아 그, 뭐랄까, 잠시만요. 저기 / 저기요 as a softening opener to get attention is distinctly native.

title: Phone number readout conventions
observed_issue: Reads 0 as '제로'/'영' inconsistently, says 공일공 vs reading clusters as large numbers
native_expectation: Reads digit-by-digit in Sino with 공 for 0 (공일공 = 010); 1588 read 일오팔팔. Korean uses 공, not 영 or 제로, on the phone.
human_note:
영(Yeong) is used in math, temperature, scores  while 공(Gong) is mainly used when reading phone numbers, bank account numbers, vehicle plate numbers, and so on
 Example: 010 is read as “gong-il-gong” (공일공).

title: Sino- vs native number system confusion
observed_issue: Picks one system; says 세 시간 as 삼 시간, or counts items with Sino (일, 이, 삼 개)
native_expectation: Hours use native (세 시간, 한 시), minutes use Sino (삼십 분); 두 명, 세 개 (native + counter) vs 삼 번, 오 층 (Sino). Mixing within one phrase (세 시 삼십 분) is the native default.
human_note: This is an important and tricky part of Korean involving the native vs. Sino-Korean numeral distinction.

title: Currency amounts in 만/억 grouping
observed_issue: Reads large won by Western thousands grouping (오십 천 원 for 50,000)
native_expectation: Groups by 만: 50,000 = 오만 원, 150,000 = 십오만 원, 1,200,000 = 백이십만 원. 오십 천 원 is impossible for a native. 원 always Sino.

title: Rising 네? vs flat 네
observed_issue: Produces flat intonation on 네 regardless, losing the question/agreement distinction
native_expectation: 네 (flat) = yes/agreement; 네? (sharp rise) = 'sorry, what?'; 네~ (long fall) = soft acknowledgment. A flat 네 where 네? is needed misfires the turn.

title: Wrong or omitted counters (분류사)
observed_issue: Drops counters or uses 개 for everything (사람 두 개, 표 한 개)
native_expectation: Selects the right counter: 두 분/두 명 (people, 분 honorific), 한 장 (tickets/cards), 한 건 (cases/bookings), 한 통 (calls). 예약 한 건, 항공권 두 장.

title: Translationese for core service nouns
observed_issue: Calques English: '비행' for flight, '북킹' or '리저베이션', '리펀드', '캔슬'
native_expectation: Uses established terms: 항공편 (flight), 예약 (booking), 환불 (refund), 취소 (cancellation), 변경 (change), 수수료 (fee). A calque instantly marks non-native.
human_note: 캔슬(Cancel) is commonly used by Koreans in everyday conversation.

title: Name order and title attachment
observed_issue: Western first-last order; attaches 씨 to family name only (김씨), or uses 씨 where service requires 고객님/님
native_expectation: Family name first (김길동); agent addresses customer as 고객님 or 길동 님, never 김 씨 alone (rude). Service register strongly prefers 고객님.

title: Sentence-final -요 rise vs fall (statement vs question)
observed_issue: Uses uniform intonation so 환불 됐어요 (statement) and 환불 됐어요? (question) sound identical
native_expectation: Korean often marks yes/no questions by rising intonation alone with identical -요 wording; the fall/rise on the final -요 distinguishes confirming vs asking (가능해요↘ vs 가능해요↗).

title: Konglish loanwords that ARE native vs over-correction
observed_issue: Either avoids all loanwords (says 표 awkwardly) or invents wrong ones
native_expectation: Uses naturalized loanwords where they're the norm: 마일리지, 체크인, 게이트, 포인트, 클레임 — but native words for 예약/환불/취소/좌석/창가. Knowing which slot takes the loanword is the skill.
human_note: The key skill is knowing which slot the loanword fits into. In Korean, both “표” and “ticket” are commonly used.

title: Date format and reading (유월/시월)
observed_issue: Says dates in English order or uses native numbers for the day; reads month names wrong
native_expectation: Year-month-day, all Sino: 이천이십육년 유월 이십삼일. June=유월, October=시월 (irregular, not 육월/십월). Getting 유월/시월 right is a strong native marker.
human_note: The pronunciations of “유월” (June) and “시월” (October) are irregular and serve as an important indicator of native vs. non-native distinction.

title: Repeated use of overly formal greetings
observed_issue: The caller unnaturally repeated overly polite expressions, such as "안녕하십니까" mid-conversation
native_expectation: "안녕하십니까" was used only once, at the start of the conversation.
example: "안녕하십니까" was used only once, at the start of the conversation.
human_note: "안녕하십니까"(greeting phrase) was used 4 times in the conversation.

native_expectation: 5월 17일

title: 措辞 for cancel: 取消 vs 退订 vs 改签
observed_issue: Uses one blanket word (取消) for refunding, changing, and cancelling, calquing English 'cancel'.
native_expectation: Distinguishes: 取消 (void an order), 退订/退票 (cancel-and-refund), 改签 (change flight), 退款 (get money back). 取消航班 implies the airline cancelled the flight, not the customer.

title: Dates with 号 and year read digit-by-digit
observed_issue: Reads 2025 as 两千零二十五, or uses 日 in speech.
native_expectation: Years read digit-by-digit: 2025年 → 二〇二五年. Spoken dates use 号 not 日: 6月23号. 日 (rì) is written/formal.

title: Request softeners 麻烦/帮我/可以…吗
observed_issue: Issues bare imperatives modeled on English ('Cancel my booking') → 取消我的订单, sounding demanding.
native_expectation: Frames requests with softeners: 麻烦您帮我…, 我想…不知道可以吗, 能不能…. Thanks with 谢谢/辛苦了.

title: Translationese connectors and pronoun overuse
observed_issue: Over-translates English structure: explicit subject pronouns every clause (我想要…我需要…我有…), 'because…so' as 因为…所以… in full each time.
native_expectation: Drops redundant pronouns (topic-prominent: 票订好了，想改一下), uses 请问/麻烦您 to open requests, and uses only 因为 OR 所以. Prefers 想 over 我想要 stacks.

title: Sentence-final particles 吧/呢/啊/嘛
observed_issue: Either omits all sentence-final particles (clipped, textbook) or sprinkles 吗 on sentences that already have a question word.
native_expectation: Uses 吧 for softened suggestions (那就改到周五吧), 呢 for follow-up questions (那退款呢？), 啊 to soften (好啊). Never 吗 with an existing interrogative; 嘛 marks 'obviously'.

title: Spelling/confirming Chinese names by character decomposition
observed_issue: Reads names letter-by-letter in pinyin or just states the syllables, unable to disambiguate homophones.
native_expectation: Disambiguates by decomposition: 弓长张 (the 张 made of 弓+长) vs 立早章; 木子李. Or '国家的国'. Surname first.

title: Phone/code digit readout: 幺 for 1, 两 for 2
observed_issue: Reads phone numbers and codes digit-by-digit as 一 (yī) for every 1 and 二 (èr) for 2.
native_expectation: On the phone, 1 is read 幺 (yāo) to avoid confusion with 七: 13800138000 → 幺三八零零幺三八零零零. Zero is 零 (líng).

title: Money: 块/毛 in speech vs 元/角 in writing
observed_issue: Says 元 (yuán) and 角 (jiǎo) aloud, or appends a stray measure word.
native_expectation: Colloquial speech uses 块 (kuài) for yuan and 毛 (máo) for jiao: 三百二十块五, 两块五毛. 元/角 sound like reading a written receipt aloud.

title: 了 for completed/changed state
observed_issue: Omits aspectual 了 (le) where a state change occurred (我收到邮件 instead of 我收到邮件了).
native_expectation: Marks completion with 了: 我已经付款了, 航班取消了, 好了. Missing 了 makes completed actions sound like generic statements.

title: Domain-specific measure words, not default 个
observed_issue: Overuses 个 (gè) for everything: 一个票, 一个航班, 一个行李.
native_expectation: Selects the right classifier: 一张票/机票 (zhāng), 一个航班 or 一班飞机 (bān), 一件行李 (jiàn), 一位 (wèi, polite for people), 一笔退款/费用 (bǐ, for sums), 一份订单 (fèn).
human_note: “一架航班” sounds better than "一个航班“

title: Native hesitation fillers vs English-style ones
observed_issue: Inserts 'um/uh', or over-literal 好的好的好的, or written 那么 as a filler.
native_expectation: Uses 那个 (nèige) and 这个 as hesitation fillers, 就是 as a stall, 嗯 as a thinking sound, 然后 to chain. e.g. 那个…我想问一下.

title: 买 mǎi vs 卖 mài (buy vs sell)
observed_issue: Produces the wrong tone, saying 卖 (mài, sell) when meaning 买 (mǎi, buy) — reversing who does what.
native_expectation: Keeps them distinct: 我想买一张票 (I want to buy a ticket) vs 卖 (sell). A tone flip here yields a real, wrong word.

title: Native airline/CS terms vs English-calqued ones
observed_issue: Code-switches or calques: says 'flight' / 'booking' / 'refund', or invents 飞行 for flight.
native_expectation: Uses established terms: 航班 (flight), 预订/订票 (booking), 退款 (refund), 改签 (rebook/change), 退票 (ticket refund), 值机 (check-in), 登机牌 (boarding pass), 订单号 (order number).

title: 二 vs 两 before measure words and amounts
observed_issue: Says 二个人, 二张票, 二点钟, 二百块 by mapping the digit 2 directly.
native_expectation: Uses 两 (liǎng) before measure words and most quantities: 两个人, 两张票, 两点 (2 o'clock), 两百块. 二 (èr) is only the bare digit/ordinal: 第二, 二楼.

title: 您 vs 你 in service register
observed_issue: Defaults to flat 你 (nǐ) throughout, sounding blunt to an agent.
native_expectation: Caller and agent both lean on 您 (nín) in service calls: 您好, 请问您…. Pure 你 reads as curt.

title: Verbalizing email @ and . natively
observed_issue: Says English 'at' and 'dot', or literal 在 / 点点 for @ and the dot.
native_expectation: @ spoken as '艾特' (àitè) or 'at'; dot is 点 (diǎn). e.g. abc@gmail.com → 'a-b-c 艾特 gmail 点 com'. Underscore _ is 下划线, hyphen - is 横杠/减号.

native_expectation: Reads record locators letter-by-letter, clarifying with 大写 (uppercase); reads separators - as 杠/横杠, / as 斜杠; uses 幺 for 1 inside codes. e.g. 订单号是 A 幺 三 杠 七.
